verses.1: The human knew his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "I have gotten a man with the help of the LORD."
verses.2: She gave birth again to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of flocks, and Cain became a tiller of the ground.
verses.3: After some time had passed, Cain brought an offering to the LORD from the fruit of the ground.
verses.4: Abel also brought an offering, from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat portions. The LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering.
verses.5: But he did not look with favor on Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and his face fell.
verses.6: The LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?
verses.7: If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin lies in wait at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it."
verses.8: Cain spoke to his brother Abel while they were in the field. Then Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
verses.9: The LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" He said, "I do not know. Am I my brother's guardian?"
verses.10: The LORD said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground.
verses.11: And now you are cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
verses.12: When you work the ground, it will no longer yield to you its strength. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."
verses.13: Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is too great to bear.
verses.14: Today you have driven me away from the presence of the ground, and I will be hidden from your face. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
verses.15: The LORD said to him, "Then whoever kills Cain, vengeance will be taken from him sevenfold." And the LORD set a mark on Cain, so that no one finding him would kill him.
verses.16: So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
verses.17: Cain knew his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city and named the city after his son Enoch.
verses.18: Enoch fathered Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
verses.19: Lamech took two wives. The name of the first was Adah, and the name of the second was Zillah.
verses.20: Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the ancestor of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.
verses.21: His brother's name was Jubal, who was the ancestor of all who play the lyre and the flute.
verses.22: Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-Cain, the forger of every tool of bronze and iron. The sister of Tubal-Cain was Naamah.
verses.23: Lamech said to his wives, Adah and Zillah, "Hear my voice, wives of Lamech, listen to what I say. I have killed a man for wounding me, and a boy for striking me.
verses.24: For if Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold."
verses.25: Adam knew his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, "God has given me another seed in place of Abel, for Cain killed him."
verses.26: To Seth also was born a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time people began to call upon the name of the LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 7: "sin lies in wait at the door" — the Hebrew uses a metaphor of a crouching animal, "chattat rovet," which is rendered as "sin lies in wait at the door."
- v. 23: "I have killed a man for wounding me, and a boy for striking me" — the Hebrew uses poetic parallelism to emphasize the escalation from wounding to death.
- v. 26: "people began to call upon the name of the LORD" — the phrase "to call upon the name of YHWH" is a standard biblical idiom for worship or invoking divine presence.
raw:
[1] The human knew his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "I have gotten a man with the help of the LORD."

[2] She gave birth again to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of flocks, and Cain became a tiller of the ground.

[3] After some time had passed, Cain brought an offering to the LORD from the fruit of the ground.

[4] Abel also brought an offering, from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat portions. The LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering.

[5] But he did not look with favor on Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and his face fell.

[6] The LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?

[7] If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin lies in wait at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it."

[8] Cain spoke to his brother Abel while they were in the field. Then Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.

[9] The LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" He said, "I do not know. Am I my brother's guardian?"

[10] The LORD said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground.

[11] And now you are cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.

[12] When you work the ground, it will no longer yield to you its strength. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."

[13] Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is too great to bear.

[14] Today you have driven me away from the presence of the ground, and I will be hidden from your face. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."

[15] The LORD said to him, "Then whoever kills Cain, vengeance will be taken from him sevenfold." And the LORD set a mark on Cain, so that no one finding him would kill him.

[16] So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

[17] Cain knew his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city and named the city after his son Enoch.

[18] Enoch fathered Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.

[19] Lamech took two wives. The name of the first was Adah, and the name of the second was Zillah.

[20] Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the ancestor of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.

[21] His brother's name was Jubal, who was the ancestor of all who play the lyre and the flute.

[22] Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-Cain, the forger of every tool of bronze and iron. The sister of Tubal-Cain was Naamah.

[23] Lamech said to his wives, Adah and Zillah, "Hear my voice, wives of Lamech, listen to what I say. I have killed a man for wounding me, and a boy for striking me.

[24] For if Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold."

[25] Adam knew his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, "God has given me another seed in place of Abel, for Cain killed him."

[26] To Seth also was born a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time people began to call upon the name of the LORD.

---
Notes
- v. 7: "sin lies in wait at the door" — the Hebrew uses a metaphor of a crouching animal, "chattat rovet," which is rendered as "sin lies in wait at the door."
- v. 23: "I have killed a man for wounding me, and a boy for striking me" — the Hebrew uses poetic parallelism to emphasize the escalation from wounding to death.
- v. 26: "people began to call upon the name of the LORD" — the phrase "to call upon the name of YHWH" is a standard biblical idiom for worship or invoking divine presence.
